Required Experience: A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in programme management, international partnership coordination, community engagement, or event design and delivery, preferably in the context of Earth observations, environmental data, sustainable development, or intergovernmental organizations.  --- Background The Group on Earth Observations (GEO) is an intergovernmental partnership that provides trusted Earth Intelligence as a public good to support evidence-based decision-making. Hosted by the World Meteorological Organization, GEO brings together 117 governments and over 160 organizations, including leading space agencies, research institutions, UN bodies, and private sector innovators. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, GEO empowers everyone, everywhere, to access and contribute to open, actionable Earth observation data; enabling better decisions for people, planet, and nature.  The GEO Work Programme (GWP) is the primary mechanism through which GEO implements its mission and strategic objectives. It is a coordinated, multi-annual portfolio of 49 activities developed and carried out by GEO Members, Participating Organizations, and partners to advance the use of Earth observations for evidence-based decision-making.  Within the GWP team, and under the supervision of the Chief, Work Programme Coordinator, the Work Programme Officer holds operational responsibility for facilitating implementation of the GEO Work Programme and driving engagement with the GEO community. This includes overseeing the GEO Community Space and other mechanisms through which GEO Members, Participating Organizations and Associates connect, collaborate, and contribute to GWP activities. The Officer designs and delivers engagement events, including the GEO Symposium, and implements the GWP Monitoring and Evaluation Framework, so that community engagement and evidence of impact strengthen the coherence, uptake, and visibility of the GWP.  Duties and Responsibilities The Work Programme Officer will be responsible for the following duties: Serve as the principal operational focal point for the GWP community, managing relationships with activity leads and points of contact, coordinating responses to inquiries and information requests related to implementation, monitoring, reporting, and GWP-wide processes; Oversee the GEO Community Space, serving as the primary point of contact for community engagement, facilitating collaboration among GWP leads, and ensuring the Space functions as a vibrant hub for knowledge exchange and partnership building for GEO Members, Participating Organizations and Associates; Lead the design and delivery of the GWP's contribution to major GEO convenings, in particular the GEO Symposium, supporting the Programme Board and ensuring these reflect GWP priorities, showcase results, and foster meaningful participation from Members, Participating Organizations, Associates, and external partners; Assess draft Implementation Plans of candidate GWP activities against defined criteria and support the Programme Board and its M&E Taskforce in their review, acceptance, or improvement; Implement the Monitoring and Evaluation Framework for the GWP, including the development and administration of tools to collect monitoring data from GWP activities, in close coordination with the Programme Board and its M&E Taskforce; Analyse the progress, outcomes, and impact of GWP activities and prepare Progress Reports, GEO Highlights Reports, and strategic recommendations for the GEO Secretariat, Programme Board, and other GEO governance bodies; Provide governance support to the GEO Programme Board, including preparation of its meetings, related documentation, follow-ups and presentations on GWP monitoring, performance, and community engagement; Support Member Services-led engagement with GEO Members by providing tailored information, analysis, briefings, and advice on GWP activities, results, and engagement opportunities relevant to their priorities; Supervise the Partnerships Officer, Participating Organizations and Associates, including work planning, performance management, and professional development; Represent the GEO Secretariat, as delegated, in relevant intergovernmental, inter-agency, technical, and multi-stakeholder meetings, workshops, and events related to the GWP, and prepare substantive inputs, meeting summaries, and follow-up actions as required; Carry out other duties as required.  Required Skills and Experience Education:  Master's degree or equivalent in environmental sciences, international relations, public policy, social sciences or a related field. Additional qualifications in Earth observations, geospatial information or data science would be an advantage. A first-level university degree or equivalent in combination with two years of additional directly relevant experience may be accepted in lieu of the master’s degree.  Experience: A minimum of seven (7) years of progressively responsible experience in programme management, international partnership coordination, community engagement, or event design and delivery, preferably in the context of Earth observations, environmental data, sustainable development, or intergovernmental organizations. Experience in monitoring and evaluation, governance support, and leading design of multi-stakeholder convenings is highly desirable. Experience supervising staff is an asset.  Other Requirements:  Working knowledge of the United Nations or a similar international organization. Familiarity with the work of the GEO Secretariat. Familiarity with scientific and technical concepts related to Earth observations, with the ability to convey complex concepts to non-specialist audiences. Ability to draft reports, correspondence and documents clearly and succinctly in English. Strong problem-solving skills and flexibility to adapt to changing requirements. Skills in collaboration, negotiation, and maintaining partnerships. Demonstrated ability to take initiative, plan, and manage multiple workloads. Ability to work in a multicultural environment and foster diversity and team spirit.  Languages: Excellent knowledge of English (both oral and written). Knowledge of other official languages of the Organization would be an advantage. Note: The working language of the GEO Secretariat is English. (Note: the official languages of the Organization are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish.).  Competencies The Work Programme Officer must demonstrate managerial-level proficiency in the following competencies: Communication & Influence Collaboration & Team Dynamics Inclusive Mindset & Cultural Awareness Decision Making & Problem Solving Integrity & Accountability Innovation & Digital Agility Stakeholder Understanding & Engagement  Salary and Allowances: The position is funded from extra-budgetary funding. Annual net base salary on initial appointment is: US$ 86,027 Annual post adjustment on initial salary is: US$ 72,521 (in addition to the net base salary)  Additional Information: The GEO Secretariat is committed to achieving diversity and a balanced workforce. Applications are welcome from qualified women and men, including those with disabilities. The statutory retirement age is 65. Pursuant to WMO Standing Instructions, the minimum age to be eligible for consideration for vacant positions is 18, and the maximum age must enable the candidate to serve for at least the term of the contract before reaching mandatory age of separation.  Probation Possibility of renewal subject to the availability of funds and pending satisfactory performance after an initial probationary period of one year which can be extended up to a maximum of two years.  Applications: Applications should be made online through the WMO e-recruitment system. Do not send your application via multiple routes. The GEO Secretariat no longer accepts applications via post or email. Only applicants for whom the GEO Secretariat has further interest will be contacted. Shortlisted candidates may be required to sit a written test and/or an interview.  Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority The GEO Secretariat does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.  Scam alert The GEO Secretariat does not charge a processing fee at any stage of its recruitment, selection, and hiring processes (i.e., application stage, interview stage, validation stage, or appointment and training). The GEO Secretariat will not ask for applicants’ bank account information.

4461229170.desc: Location: Stans, NW, Switzerland Apply now What you can expect Join us in shaping how AI changes the way ROSEN works. This role is not about introducing new tools. It is about helping people rethink how work gets done and creating the capabilities that turn AI potential into measurable business impact. As AI Education & Training Program Lead, you will own and scale ROSEN's AI Enablement Program across approximately 4'500 employees worldwide. Your mission is to build the skills, confidence, and structures that enable employees to move from basic AI literacy to meaningful workflow transformation while maintaining human accountability and compliance requirements. You will define learning standards, establish certification paths, create a scalable train-the-trainer approach, and build a network of champions and facilitators who multiply adoption across the organization. Rather than delivering training yourself at scale, you will create the system that enables others to do so effectively. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys designing learning experiences, facilitating workshops, building communities and driving change across a global organization. You will take the program from its current foundation to enterprise-wide adoption and continuous growth. You will lead the AI Enablement Program from strategy to execution and continuously evolve it as AI capabilities and business needs mature. Your responsibilities include: Driving the end-to-end AI enablement strategy and ensuring consistent delivery across all learning and certification tracks Establishing and maintaining training standards, certification requirements and learning pathways for different employee groups Building, certifying, and supporting a global network of facilitators, trainers and AI Champions Growing and moderating the AI Network as a platform for collaboration, learning and knowledge sharing Creating and sustaining Communities of Practice that encourage employees to share experiences, use cases and best practices Defining and monitoring success metrics that measure both participation and business impact Ensuring AI literacy and training programs align with legal, governance, security and compliance requirements, including the EU AI Act Preparing and supporting program steering activities and providing transparency on progress, adoption, and outcomes Collaborating closely with Learning & Development, IT, Security, Legal, Compliance, Data & AI Governance and business stakeholders Leading workshops, facilitating discussions and guiding teams through the organizational changes required to successfully adopt AI What you will bring You are passionate about helping people develop new capabilities and can translate emerging technologies into practical value for employees and the business. You combine strong program leadership with hands-on facilitation skills and are comfortable operating in a dynamic transformation environment. You bring: Experience leading large-scale learning, capability-building, or enablement programs across multiple functions and regions The ability to design structured learning journeys with clear progression paths and measurable outcomes Strong facilitation skills and practical experience building train-the-trainer or similar multiplier models A solid understanding of Generative AI, Large Language Models and modern AI tools Experience managing organizational change and supporting teams through evolving ways of working A data-driven mindset and the ability to define, track, and communicate meaningful success metrics The ability to influence stakeholders, align competing priorities, and maintain momentum without formal authority Confidence working in complex technical environments where quality, safety and reliability are critical A proactive, entrepreneurial mindset with a strong sense of ownership and accountability Professional proficiency in German and English, both written and spoken Nice to have: Experience building and scaling an enterprise AI or digital transformation enablement program Experience developing certification frameworks and linking them to employee development and proficiency models Proven success establishing and growing Communities of Practice or internal expert networks Familiarity with workflow redesign, continuous discovery, service design, or Jobs-to-be-Done methodologies Experience working in industrial, engineering, technology, or other complex operational environments. What we offer We offer you an exciting and varied task in a highly interesting and international environment with appropriate resources. You can expect advanced working conditions in an innovative and future-oriented company. Who we are The ROSEN Group is a leading global provider of cutting-edge solutions in all areas of the integrity process chain. Since its beginnings as a one-man business in 1981, ROSEN has grown rapidly and is today a technology group that operates in more than 110 countries with over 4,000 highly qualified employees. ROSEN’s products and services: Inspection of critical industrial assets to ensure reliable operations of the highest standards and effectiveness Customized engineering consultancy providing efficient asset integrity management Production and supply of customized novel products and systems Market-driven, topical state-of-the-art research and development providing “added-value” products and services For more information about the ROSEN Group, go to www.rosen-group.com. Do you have any questions? Dan Heiter Recruitment

As a trusted and respected partner to the pharmaceutical industry, we uphold the highest standards in safety, quality and sustainability, while fostering a culture that empowers you to thrive. Join a rapidly expanding global company, where diverse perspectives and experiences come together in a collaborative environment. Here, you'll find a workplace that values both collective success and your individual contributions—offering long-term opportunities to grow and make an impact. 4469882917.desc: Role: Senior Space Systems Engineer Location: Lausanne, Switzerland Contract: Permanent contract, full-time position Salary: It will be discussed during the recruiting process, taking into consideration seniority and responsibilities within the activity.  AYES is a Switzerland-based Engineering and Technology company headquartered in Baden. Our core business operates across several industrial sectors, including Automotive, Aerospace, Railway, Energy, and Life Sciences. With a strong focus on innovation and engineering excellence, AYES supports clients across Switzerland, Europe, and the United States, delivering advanced R&D and technology solutions. At AYES, people are at the center of everything we do. We believe that knowledge sharing, collaboration, and talent development are key drivers of sustainable growth and technological progress.  Key Responsibilities Lead system engineering activities across the full spacecraft lifecycle, from early concept and requirements definition through development, AIV/T, launch and in orbit commissioning. Manage key system engineering activities including functional analysis, concept of operations, mission analysis, system modes, requirements, interfaces, engineering databases and system budgets. Coordinate subsystem and software development, ensuring technical consistency, effective interface management and alignment across spacecraft and Ground Segment. Lead technical assessments, trade off studies, risk and opportunity resolution, system baseline definition and change control, while maintaining the required engineering documentation. Define and coordinate system development, verification and validation planning, support technical schedule and cost activities, and contribute to the continuous improvement of system engineering processes. Our Ideal Candidate Should Have BSc or MSc in Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, Physics or a related technical discipline. At least 8 years of experience in the spacecraft industry, with strong hands on experience in spacecraft system engineering. Strong experience in system requirements decomposition, interface management, trade studies, system sizing and performance or error budget development. Solid experience across the spacecraft development lifecycle, including design, development, verification, AIT, launch and in orbit operations. Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary technical activities and interface with customers, with knowledge in one or more spacecraft domains such as avionics, power, AOCS, propulsion, thermal and mechanical, AIT, operations, launcher interfaces or FDIR.   If you are motivated by structured engineering environments, digital process optimization, and working on complex aerospace systems, and you want to join a dynamic international engineering company with projects across Europe and the USA, then… SAY YES AND GROW WITH AYES!

4466073851.desc: Le Rôle Nous recherchons un(e) Directeur(trice) de programmes / Program Manager Senior disposant d'une solide expérience dans le pilotage de programmes complexes et stratégiques, acquise notamment au sein du secteur public. Vous prenez en charge la structuration, la gouvernance et le pilotage de programmes impliquant de multiples projets, parties prenantes et dépendances. Vous assurez une vision consolidée des enjeux, des risques, des ressources, des budgets et des échéances et accompagnez les instances de direction dans les arbitrages nécessaires. Les programmes concernés évoluent notamment dans des environnements IT, de transformation et de sécurité de l'information. Une expérience en cybersécurité, protection des données ou conformité constitue donc un atout, mais le cœur du rôle reste avant tout le management de programmes. Responsabilités  Pilotage de programmes complexes  Prendre en charge le pilotage global de programmes stratégiques composés de plusieurs projets et chantiers interdépendants.  Définir et structurer la gouvernance, les objectifs, les jalons, les livrables et les indicateurs de performance.  Piloter les budgets, ressources, plannings, risques, dépendances et priorités à l'échelle du programme.  Maintenir une vision consolidée de l'avancement et anticiper les écarts, risques et points de blocage.  Identifier les arbitrages nécessaires et accompagner les instances décisionnelles dans leur prise de décision.  Garantir la cohérence et l'alignement des différents projets avec les objectifs stratégiques du programme.  Gouvernance et coordination  Mettre en place et animer les instances de gouvernance, comités de programme et comités de pilotage.  Coordonner un large éventail de parties prenantes : directions métiers, IT, experts, responsables de projets, partenaires externes et sponsors.  Produire des reportings consolidés à destination du management et des instances décisionnelles.  Assurer une communication claire sur l'avancement, les risques, les décisions et les priorités.  Définir et faire appliquer les méthodes et standards de gestion de programme.  Gestion des risques et transformation  Identifier, évaluer et suivre les risques à l'échelle du programme.  Piloter les plans d'actions et mesures correctives nécessaires.  Accompagner les transformations organisationnelles liées aux programmes.  Contribuer à l'amélioration continue des méthodes, outils et processus de pilotage.  Environnements sécurité et conformité Selon Les Programmes Concernés  Collaborer avec les équipes en charge de la sécurité de l'information, de la protection des données et de la conformité.  Intégrer les contraintes réglementaires et de sécurité dans le pilotage des programmes.  Faciliter la coordination entre experts techniques, métiers et instances décisionnelles. Ce Que Nous Recherchons  Expérience  Expérience senior et significative en tant que Program Manager, Directeur de programmes ou fonction équivalente.  Expérience démontrée dans le pilotage de programmes complexes et stratégiques, au-delà de la gestion d'un projet individuel.  Maîtrise de la gouvernance de programmes comportant plusieurs projets, équipes et parties prenantes.  Expérience significative dans le secteur public ou auprès d'administrations / organismes publics.  Habitude de travailler avec des instances de direction et de gouvernance et de gérer des environnements comportant de nombreuses parties prenantes.  Expérience du pilotage de budgets, ressources, risques, dépendances et indicateurs de performance.  Compétences clés  Excellente maîtrise du management de programme et du pilotage multi-projets.
